caller_context_currency.reason: These models take their money fact from the caller's environment company while their owning company is not that caller, so a document created in one company context while pointing at another company's object can start with a currency that does not belong to its owning company. The divergence appears in three shapes and the list carries all three: (a) company_id is a related field derived from an owning relation (project/plan/contract), (b) the model has no company_id column at all and therefore no company of its own to own the currency (project.settlement, sc.business.fact.mixin and the two material line models), and (c) the model inherits the caller-context currency from the sc.business.fact.mixin carrier without declaring its own currency_id (sc.dashboard.cockpit.fact, sc.workbench.item, sc.document.admin.document, sc.office.admin.document, sc.hr.payroll.document). sc.treasury.ledger is listed because its readonly company_id is written by the projection, so the row company can differ from the caller. The single source for the money fact is the owning company's currency; the per-model migration changes which value an existing record carries, so it is recorded here for a product decision instead of being silently rewritten.

currency_write_paths.reason: A currency_id assignment inside a method overwrites the money fact after the field default ran, so it is a second money-fact source that a field-default-only scan cannot see. Every such assignment on a product model is registered here: four copy the currency of the owning document or ledger (single source, no divergence), sc.settlement.order fills the header from its contract in two places, and sc.norm.catalog is the one open alignment because it copies the region country currency instead of a company fact, which can leave the tenant standard currency.

The company currency pin keeps the tenant on CNY; the owner must decide whether this write path stays or the currency derives from a company fact
the red-flush snapshot copies the money fact of its original ledger entry, so the ledger stays the single source
the receipt copies the money fact of the payment request it registers, so the request stays the single source
both header-fill onchanges take the money fact from the selected contract, so the contract stays the single source; two write sites on one model are recorded so a third cannot appear unnoticed

company_field_overrides.reason: A company_id or currency_id redefined by an extension class (an _inherit class without _name) replaces the definition of the model's own class. It is registered so a redefinition stays a decision instead of a silent override.

duplicate_field_declarations.reason: A field declared by two class blocks on the same model is not a harmless duplicate: Odoo merges the definitions attribute by attribute, so the surviving field is a union of both and neither file alone shows the real declaration. A reader who edits one file cannot see the other's contribution, which makes the second declaration a hidden second source for the same fact. Every such pair in the product modules is registered here; an undeclared one, a registration whose declaring files changed, and a registration that no longer matches source all fail closed in scripts/verify/fact_source_coverage_guard.py. This is the declaration-layer companion of company_field_overrides, which owns the money-field question of where the effective definition comes from.

company_currency_write_sites.reason: res.company.currency_id is the carrier of the tenant standard currency, and it is written from three shapes that no single scan sees together: an XML record on res.company, a method on a class that extends the company model, and a module-level bootstrap function that resolves res.company and writes the field through a vals dict. Reading only the method-assignment shape hid the XML records and the bootstrap write, so all sites are named here and compared as one set; one of them is the named company_currency_authority, which keeps the declaration below from resting on a site this registry does not know.

sites.reason: the fresh-database bootstrap sets the main company to base.CNY while the same file activates base.CNY, so the installed tenant starts on the standard currency
the post-init hook writes the resolved standard currency onto every company and refuses to switch once account.move.line rows exist, so an existing accounting fact is never overwritten
the product module restates the standard currency on the main company and then calls the authority function, so an install without the bootstrap module still lands on CNY
the named authority: it activates base.CNY and moves every company without journal items onto it, skipping companies that already own accounting facts

company_currency_authority.reason: The statement that a caller-context default still resolves to the tenant standard currency depends on this pin: it makes CNY active and sets every company without journal items to it, skipping companies that already own accounting facts. The guard fails if this method disappears, stops naming the standard currency, or if standard-currency models are declared without a registered authority.

state_fact.reason: A record lifecycle is a fact. It was declared in four places at once: the ScStateMachine tables, a second table copied next to one model, ad-hoc 'if state not in (...)' checks inside each action, and the workflow profile map. Whichever one a writer happened to consult became the truth, so a caller could write a state the declared table forbids. The table is now the single declared source and this registry records, per registered model, where that table is actually consulted, which models only borrow a lifecycle Selection, which second tables exist and why, and every site that writes state under an explicit bypass so a bypass stays a decision, not a habit.

enforcements.reason: write() refuses any state change that is not the lifecycle-service call, and _write_lifecycle now reads the declared ScStateMachine.SETTLEMENT_ORDER table instead of a private copy, so the guard and the table cannot drift apart again.
write() refuses a bare state write and asserts ScStateMachine.GENERAL_CONTRACT on every declared writer, so the published ladder (draft->confirmed->signed) is the only one the model accepts.

write() refuses a bare state write and asserts ScStateMachine.CONTRACT on every declared writer, so closed/cancel are the terminal states the table declares rather than whatever an action happened to allow.
write() refuses a bare state write and asserts ScStateMachine.SETTLEMENT on the three action writers, so the declared ladder is the one fact instead of the three per-action if-checks.
